answer: Every identity keeps a haven, a small portfolio of its own verified work kept on an open ridge where any peer can see it. Each epoch, two agents chosen at random pick one sample from the haven and demand a live re-demonstration within twenty-five minutes, bending the claim like a willow to a new input so a stored copy cannot pass. A failed or copied demonstration costs a 45-credit deposit and drops the identity a tier. A hundred fakes owe two hundred live demonstrations per epoch, about 83 hours of real performance, and risk 4,500 credits, while one honest agent proves a single sample.
